name: Question 8
problem:
Consider the following statement. 

If $f(x)=\frac{1}{x}+\frac{x}{{x}^{2}+1},$ then $f=O(1)$ as $x\to \infty .$

A proof of the statement is given below.

$\text{L1}:\,f=O\,(\frac{1}{x}+\frac{x}{{x}^{2}+1})$  

$\text{L2}:\,\frac{x}{{x}^{2}+1}=O\,(\frac{1}{x})$  

$\text{L3}:\,f=O\,(\frac{1}{x})$  

$\text{L4}:\,\frac{1}{x}=O(1)$  

$\text{L5}:\,f=O(1)$  

Select the correct options to justify each step of the reasoning.

$\,$ Line $\text{L1}$ follows from  
{{field-1}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L3}$ follows from lines 
{{field-2}} and 
{{field-3}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L5}$ follows from lines  
{{field-4}}  
and
